related_questions.question: How to retrain smell after COVID?

text_blocks.snippet: To retrain your sense of smell after COVID-19, a technique called smell retraining can be used. This involves daily exposure to specific scents to help stimulate and restore your olfactory receptors.
snippet_highlighted_words: daily exposure to specific scents to help stimulate and restore your olfactory receptors

text_blocks.snippet: Here's how to perform smell retraining:

list.title: 1. Gather your scents:
list.snippet: Use four essential oils: rose, citronella (or lemon), eucalyptus, and cinnamon.

list.title: 2. Prepare the oils:
list.snippet: Place a few drops of each oil on a cotton ball or pad and let it sit for a minute or two.

list.title: 3. Smell each oil:
list.snippet: Bring the cotton ball close to your nose (about an inch away) and inhale slowly and naturally.

list.title: 4. Visualize:
list.snippet: While inhaling, try to visualize the scent or look at a picture of the item associated with the scent.

list.title: 5. Repeat:
list.snippet: Repeat the process with each oil, taking a few minutes to rest between each scent.

list.title: 6. Frequency:
list.snippet: Perform this process twice a day for six weeks.

text_blocks.snippet: By consistently exposing your olfactory system to these scents, you may be able to retrain your sense of smell and potentially regain some or all of your lost ability to smell.
